title: An Analysis of the United States Cyber Insurance Industry
content: Cyber insurance is gaining faster adoption by businesses to cover their losses, but it transfers only selected financial losses. The protection a business receives depends on the wording of its contract and the conditions imposed during underwriting. To highlight current challenges, this review brings together academic literature, National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) reports, and material concerning top insurers active in the U.S. market. It compares the losses addressed by their policies, the restrictions on payment, and the security requirements applied to prospective policyholders. The review also considers how security-rating services support these decisions. The comparison points to a distinction between the range of benefits described in a policy and the protection available once triggers, sublimits, deductibles, and exclusions are applied. Differences in terminology and assessment practices make this distinction difficult for buyers to evaluate. Affordability for smaller firms and losses affecting many insured businesses at once remain important concerns in the reviewed evidence. The paper presents possible responses around technology, underwriting, pricing and policy collaboration, education and prevention, and supporting services. These recommendations offer a basis for further investigation; the review does not test their effects on premiums, claims, or cybersecurity outcomes.
